subject: Arabic Language

source.title: Primary School Education Curriculum Design — Arabic Language Grade 6 (First Published 2017, Revised 2024)
source.url: User-supplied local file (grade-6-curriculum-desings/GRADE-6-ARABIC-Curriculum-Designs.pdf); no confirmed public mirror recorded.
source.notes: Read in full via the Read tool with no `pages` parameter (native text extraction, all 77 pages). CONFIRMS the 9-theme x 3-strand = 27 sub-strand architecture shared with French/German/Mandarin/Arabic Grade 7-9 (Greetings and Introduction, Family, My Surrounding, Time, Fun and Enjoyment, Food and Drinks, Body Parts/My Body, Weather and Environment, Getting Around) — verified directly from the document body (Strand 1.0 pp.13-32, Strand 2.0 pp.33-52, Strand 3.0 pp.53-72), not just the p.xii 'SUMMARY OF STRANDS AND SUBSTRANDS' aggregation table (which groups by sub-strand NAME, e.g. 'Phonological awareness: Pronunciation' appears twice at 1.1 and 1.6, summing to 4 lessons in the summary — this is the same aggregation-table trap flagged in Grade 8 Arabic's sourcing notes; the per-theme tables were used as the source of truth here, not the summary). Grade 6 is Upper Primary (not Junior School) and its essence statement differs from the sibling grades only in the final clause: 'The learner will transit to Junior School having acquired basic proficiency equivalent to A1/YCT2' (vs 'transit to Senior School' in Grade 8/9). KEY CONTENT-DEPTH FINDING: unlike Grade 7/8 Arabic, this Grade 6 design gives very few concrete named Arabic words/phrases in its Suggested Learning Experiences columns — it is markedly more meta/process-oriented (activities like 'listen to an audio recording', 'peer assess', 'role play') rather than supplying specific vocabulary items. The concrete content it DOES name verbatim is: the four short vowel signs/harakat (fatha, kasra, dhama, sukun) at 1.1; nunation/tanween at 1.3 and 2.3; shaddah-emphasis example words 'sabburah, Allah, baddah' at 1.4; long vowel/madda at 1.5 and 2.5; makhariju huruf (articulation points/phonetics) at 1.7; the English-language example greeting register 'good morning, good afternoon, good evening' at 1.1; the English-language example food-preference sentence 'I like rice than ugali, I don't like chips' at 1.6; the English-language example school-property sentences 'the office is closed today, the library is big' at 3.3; the English-language example sentence 'I brush my teeth every morning' at 3.7; and the position/location vocabulary set 'next to, opposite, in front, near, across' plus the worked examples 'behind the library, near the staffroom' at 1.9. All other thematic vocabulary (nuclear family member names, months of the year, games/sports names, food items, body parts, weather conditions, school facilities) is named only as a category heading (e.g. 'Vocabulary building- Nuclear family', 'Vocabulary- games and sports') without KICD supplying the actual word list — consistent with the established sibling-grade convention (see grade-8/arabic.json), the actual romanized-Arabic vocabulary items used in the shipped skills were authored to match each named category, at Grade 6's basic/foundational level, not invented beyond what the category names call for. A second structural difference from Grade 7/8: Theme 9 'Getting Around' does NOT carry transport vocabulary at Grade 6 (unlike the G7/G8 sibling pattern) — its actual content is 1.9 Language Use (locating objects/positions), 2.9 Extensive Reading (library skills/reading logs), and 3.9 Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing (describing school facilities); the shipped Grade 6 skills follow this actual mined content rather than assuming a transport theme by analogy to G7/G8. Suggested Learning Experiences, Core Competencies, Values, PCIs and Links to Other Learning Areas were all read in full per the mining guide's 8-part checklist and are captured below via `learningExperiences`, `coreCompetencies`, `linkedLearningAreas` and `scopeNotes`. Assessment rubrics (pp.31-32 Listening & Speaking, pp.51-52 Reading, pp.71-72 Writing) were reviewed — all describe the same 4-band Exceeds/Meets/Approaches/Below Expectation structure as the sibling grades, no sub-strand-specific content beyond what's already captured. Appendix 1 (p.73-75) describes the annual Community Service Learning (CSL) project (Whole School Approach, hosted in Social Studies) and Appendix 2 (p.76-77) lists generic per-strand learning resources/assessment methods/non-formal activities (Kenya Music Festival, Arabic language Clubs, Exchange Programs, Language Days, Inter-House/Class/School Competitions) — these are cross-strand and not sub-strand-specific, so not repeated per sub-strand below. Unlike Grade 8 Arabic, this Grade 6 design has NO separate 'Showcasing of skills and concepts (Exhibition)' strand entry in the body — the summary table lists it as a standalone 6-lesson allocation (bringing the 54 sub-strand lessons + 6 = 60 total), matching the same pattern as Grade 8's Exhibition allocation, tied to the same Appendix 1 CSL project.

essenceNote: Kenya is part of the international community and therefore the learners shall be given an opportunity to learn foreign languages in addition to the national, official and indigenous languages. These foreign languages include: Arabic, French, German and Mandarin. The Learner is expected to acquire the four language skills: listening, speaking, reading and writing at a basic level in the curriculum. This will give the learner an opportunity to acquire language competencies in an experiential, innovative and flexible ways. Foreign languages learning at this level is guided by social-constructivism and environmental theories. Learning of these languages will promote international consciousness and appreciation of one's own and others' cultures. The learner will transit to Junior School having acquired basic proficiency equivalent to A1/YCT2 (verbatim from the source, p.x — note 'Junior School' here, not 'Senior School' as in the Grade 8/9 essence statements, since Grade 6 is the final year of Upper Primary).

outcomes: listen and respond appropriately to relevant information in the Arabic language,
read a wide variety of texts fluently and accurately for lifelong learning,
write texts legibly, coherently and creatively in the Arabic language,
express themselves fluently and confidently in varied contexts,

subStrands.name: Showcasing of skills and concepts (Exhibition)
subStrands.notes: Allocated 6 lessons (54 sub-strand lessons + 6 = 60 total per p.xii summary table). Not one of the 27 theme-based sub-strands above — a standalone allocation tied to the Community Service Learning (CSL) project described in Appendix 1 (p.73-75): an annual, Whole-School-Approach class project hosted in Social Studies, run in 3 steps (Preparation, Implementation, Reflection) across the school terms. No specific learning outcomes or key inquiry questions are attached to it in the source; it is assessed formatively (skills applied, core competencies, values demonstrated) rather than via a sub-strand rubric. No shipped skill file corresponds to this entry, consistent with how Grade 8 Arabic's equivalent Exhibition allocation was handled.
